### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via resumeActionRunRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via screenNodeId (symbol, a field of interface ActionResumeRequest))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c72dbb805842c4533d4e888158bc9a514c92e779` — the merge of head `85b5f360e19824f42dea785b8036c39c1caf8dbd` into base `3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c72dbb805842c4533d4e888158bc9a514c92e779 && git checkout c72dbb805842c4533d4e888158bc9a514c92e779
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6 85b5f360e19824f42dea785b8036c39c1caf8dbd && git checkout -B drift-repro 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6 && git merge --no-ff 85b5f360e19824f42dea785b8036c39c1caf8dbd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3bbda33b78fff2681db9c09732347bc62ffc4cc6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

2. **PR-body footer form (body only).** The body ends with `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)` and a bare session URL. AGENTS.md's form for a PR body is a blank line, `---`, then `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_<id>)_`. Please send that form and read the body back.

### Checklist (read on GitHub at this head, not from the report)

The premise required by the ruling, reproduction before any code, is recorded on `main` `dc66d330` in all three of the card's ways, with a single-screen control.
- **File surface:** 8 files, +386/−35. All are inside the claim's surface. No new code is minted, so the ledger is untouched, as the claim allowed.
- **Mechanism, read in the source:**
  - `refuseUnresumableAdmittedRun` now returns `{ subject, screen }`.
  - The hand-off writes `run.screenNodeId` only when the engine names a non-empty `nodeId`.
  - The host door refuses a non-string or empty `screenNodeId` with 400 before `getRun`. A valid one rides `hostDoor` into step 5, which refuses a mismatch with 409 before `automation.resume`, so nothing is consumed.
  - `screenNodeIdOf` treats a missing `nodeId` as `undefined`. A bound id against an unnamed screen is therefore refused, which fails closed. The message names both screens, or "another screen".
  - The MCP `resume_run` path without a hand-off is untouched.
- **Spec face:** `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts` changes TypeScript interface and docblock only: an optional `run.screenNodeId`, and rule-4 and service prose that replaces the "void an item whose run has moved on is the host's" sentence. No Zod schema moves. `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` matches the new door.
- **Tests:** seven `[#34515]` unit cases, and three dogfood cases over the real stack, the real engine and MCP over HTTP. The one forced change is the `[#33690]` `toEqual`, which now includes `screenNodeId: 'screen_1'`, and it is named. Two ablation legs are reported, restored to the HEAD blob and to dist.
- **Gates at this head:**
  - Check-runs on `1f37c11a…`: 68 runs, 58 `success`, 10 `skipped`, 0 failed. `Dogfood Regression Gate` (the aggregate) is `success`, and its shards were skipped by the selector, as the area said. So the new dogfood cases have local readings only. That is item 1's battery.
  - `git merge-tree --write-tree` against today's `origin/main` is clean.
  - `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34753`, read here: 0 of 8 paths governed, 421 lines.

### Owed after this

- **L2: owed, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`**, on the fixed head. The faces are non-test `packages/spec/src`, Clause-② yes, and, after item 1, a declared narrowing.
- **Landing tier: spec face and narrowing, handed to the seat for Tier H.** Not governed.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `51975cc36b11d651d783a4e7079621ede9c3b4cd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (implementing files); narrowing floor, every path of the diff outside the prose faces: the four files above plus packages/runtime/src/action-confirmation-handoff-33690.test.ts and packages/qa/dogfood/test/action-confirmation-handoff-33690.dogfood.test.ts; read in the cited code, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts (`ScreenSpec.nodeId`, `resume`, `getSuspendedScreen`), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`getSuspendedScreen`, the in-process `resuming` guard), `main`'s copy of ai-service.ts (rule 4). Prose faces read for agreement only: .changeset/34515-resume-approval-bound-to-screen.md, content/docs/ui/actions.mdx.
Security-touching: yes

Inputs read: card #34515 body and all six comments (analysis 6932866004, ruling 6942893807, claim 6943219796, registration 6943263230, dev report 6944537865, seat correction 6945347284); PR #34753 body, its 8-file list, the net diff against merge-base `6dd57163`; the 72 check-runs on this head. The L1 comments on the PR were not relied on. Resubmission check: over the PR's 8 files, the withdrawn head `1f37c11a` and this head differ in the changeset alone, and `main` moved none of the 8 files in between, so the code is the code of the withdrawn head.

Check-runs on this head: 72, all completed, none pending: 60 success, 12 skipped, 0 failed. Skipped: the `Dogfood Regression Gate` shard matrix, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance`, `UI Published Artifacts`, `Lint UI`, `Queue verdict`, `Borrowed queue verdict`, the schedule gate, the two opt-in harnesses, and the second (body-edit) runs of `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size`. `Check Changeset` success on both runs; `Test Core` 1 to 8 success; `TypeScript Type Check` success; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ActionConfirmationHandOff.run.screenNodeId` (spec, optional TypeScript member): a widening of a published contract interface. Right. Written only from the engine's `ScreenSpec.nodeId` at hand-off (`screenNodeIdOf`), never from caller input; omitted when the engine names no node. A host that ignores it sees no change.
- `ActionResumeRequest.screenNodeId` (runtime, optional): a widening. Right. Omitted or `undefined`, `hostDoor` carries no `screenNodeId`, `boundScreenNodeId` stays `undefined`, and step 5 is byte-for-byte the step 5 of `main`: "unchanged without `screenNodeId`" is true. Sent as `null`, `''` or a non-string it is refused 400 before `getRun`: that is a new answer, reachable only by a caller that sends the new key, so no call that exists today is narrowed; it fails closed.
- Name: `screenNodeId` on both keys, exactly the name the seat set in 6932866004. Right.
- Refusal: 409, code derived from the status by `deps.error` through `resumeDoorError`, no `details`, the same envelope as the sibling step-5 refusal ("paused, but not on a screen"). The unit pins read `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` at the host door and at the MCP bridge, and `Test Core` is green. No code minted, ledger untouched. Right, and as the seat approved.
- Compare, read in `refuseUnresumableAdmittedRun`: a supplied id against a current screen with no `nodeId` is a mismatch and is refused (closed); a supplied id for a run not paused on a screen is refused by the earlier 409 (closed); a supplied id equal to the current screen resumes. The compare runs before `automation.resume`, so a refusal consumes nothing. Right.
- Elicited accept (MCP `resume_run`, declared-gated flow action, form-mode elicitation): bound unconditionally to the screen read before the person was asked; a run that moved on meanwhile is refused 409 where `main` answered 200 and submitted to the other screen. A narrowing of a published door's accept set. Declared. Right as a declaration; see ③ for whose decision it is and S1 for the contract text.
- MCP `resume_run` of an action with no declared confirmation: `hostDoor` absent, no elicitation, unbound, unchanged. Right.
- Invocation row: a step-5 mismatch is thrown inside `continueAdmittedRun`, so it writes one `failed` `action_invocation` row, as every step 4 to 5 refusal already does. Unchanged rule, right.
- `action-execution.ts` (N2 of record 6932783796): the enforced-set comment now names the host resume door; it agrees with `resumeAdmissionRefusal`'s `hostConfirmation` arm. Right.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — the right single line for a diff that both widens and narrows. AGENTS.md allows `yes|no` plus at most one arm of the closed pair, and `record-recognisers.mjs` reads `yes (narrowing)` as the narrowing face ("a diff that widens and narrows owes the narrowing face's review"). The line stands on the PR body and the changeset, identically worded.

- Level: `@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/runtime` patch beside `Metadata-protocol: none`. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` grades by the metadata protocol alone: `none` takes patch on every entry, and a non-protocol breaking change ships patch with its BREAKING banner. No authorable key, value or metadata type moves, so `none` is true. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head.
- BREAKING paragraph: FROM (the accept resumed the screen the run had moved on to, with the first screen's values, as the person) and TO (409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, nothing resumes, the run stays) are both true against the code and against `main`. The one-line fix ("the agent asks again on the screen the run is on now") is present and is what the refusal message says.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: holds; nothing stored is rewritten.
- Title carries `!`. `Skills-docs: none` with its reason.
- Both published packages the diff moves are named; the dogfood package is private test code.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, elicited path bound too (deviation in 6944537865): answered in part, ESCALATED in part. Judged as a narrowing against the published spec on `main`: rule 4 says an elicited accept "covers that one call", and that call was a submit of values the agent gave for the screen the run was then on. `main` never declared "an accept resumes whichever screen the run has reached" as a capability; the 200 it gave is the very outcome the card exists to stop. So the narrowing makes the rule real and takes no declared capability from a consumer. That is the design answer. The decision answer is not this record's: option A as the maintainer read it in 6932866004 is a hand-off mechanism (two optional keys, a step-5 compare, "Clause-② yes, widening", facet ④ "only adds an optional key"), and its three cases are all pending items. The elicited cell is neither a pending item nor a widening, and it is BREAKING. The seat's correction 6945347284 is the seat's word, not the maintainer's. ESCALATED to the Tier H approval: the maintainer must be shown, and confirm, the BREAKING elicited cell as such; if it is not confirmed, the elicited binding comes out and the PR returns to the widening the ruling describes. This record does not decide it.
- Dev flag, cloud follow-up "noted, not filed": ESCALATED to the seat. The ruling's execution line for A orders a separate cloud card (store the key with the pending item and pass it back). `Fixes #34515` closes the card on merge. Until cloud passes the key back, every handed-off approval stays on the unbound path, which is fail-open with respect to the card's defect: the three reproduced cases still reproduce on a host that omits the key. Only the elicited path is closed by this repo alone. The contract cloud must satisfy is two optional keys, so cloud can adopt it with no breaking change. The cloud card must exist before this PR closes #34515.
- Dev flag, omission keeps the unbound path: answered. It is the ruling's intent (option A: optional keys), not a gap in the diff; the consequence is the bullet above.
- Dev flag, ablation leg B preflight exited 1 in-leg: a local reading, not a gate verdict; not relied on here.
- Dev flag, the dogfood fixture grew two flow actions and two flows: test code, the lane seat's ACCEPT.
- `open_questions` entry (route to the L2 seat): answered by this record.
- Out-of-scope finding, a wizard looping back to the same node (option D): answered; the limit is stated in the changeset. It is not stated in the spec or in actions.mdx (see N2).
- Security: an approval and resume gate is authorisation-adjacent. No bypass or replay is added. The new key can only add a refusal; the MCP `resume_run` input cannot carry it (`boundScreenNodeId` is read from `hostDoor` or from the engine's own screen, never from the agent's input); every existing gate (owner, admission, confirmation, subject read) is asked as before. No access finding.
- Dogfood: the three new dogfood cases and the 4058-pass full battery are local readings only. The `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards were skipped by the selector on this head, so there is no CI verdict for any dogfood case here; the aggregate job's success is the selector's, not a run of them. No dogfood case, local or CI, covers the narrowed elicited cell.
- Unit pins (CI, `Test Core` green): seven `[#34515]` cases pin the 409 on all three hand-off cases and on the elicited cell, the 400, and both controls, against an automation double. They pin the door's contract. They do not pin that the real engine serves a distinct `nodeId` per screen; `ScreenSpec.nodeId` is a required member of the automation contract, which is what the door relies on.
- SQL push-down: no query, id materialisation or in-app join is added. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts, against ruling 6942893807 (A), its first consumer (`resumeActionRun` and the host door) and the scenario on the card:

- Rule 4's hand-off bullet, the `run.screenNodeId` jsdoc and the `IActionConfirmationService` paragraph each agree with the code, sentence by sentence: recorded at hand-off from the parked screen, bound when the host passes it back, refused 409 with the run left where it is, unbound when omitted, deciding an item once left with the host. The replaced sentence ("voiding an item whose run has moved on" is the host's) is correctly gone.
- Tried to break it: a different screen id supplied by the host (refused unless it is the current screen, which is the host's own trusted call); `null` or `''` (400); an id for a run parked on a non-screen node (409 by the earlier check); a current screen with no `nodeId` (refused); the agent supplying the id (no path); a second approval after the wizard completed (404 at step 2). All closed.

S1 (should-fix) — the contract does not state the narrowing this PR declares BREAKING. In ai-service.ts rule 4, "Elicited `accept`: the call dispatches as any admitted call does, exactly once" is unchanged, and the new binding sentence is written for the hand-off alone and is conditioned on "when the host passes that screen back". The code binds an elicited accept of a `resume_run` to the screen the run was parked on when the person was asked, unconditionally, and refuses 409 otherwise. The only statements of that are the step-5 docblock in mcp.ts and the changeset.
